cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Milvus 3.0 goes lake-native, reshaping how production AI apps retrieve vector data
stories.plain: Zilliz's Milvus 3.0 lets developers build and serve production-grade vector indexes directly over data-lake storage, removing the need to copy data into a separate vector store. This changes how AI applications — including personalization and agentic systems — are architected and priced, making the open-source option more competitive with managed cloud alternatives.

stories.head: Why enterprise AI ROI disappoints — and why first-party data is the real asset
stories.plain: A practitioner-level essay argues that most enterprise AI deployments underdeliver because leaders chase tools before fixing their data foundations. The core claim: proprietary customer data — not the AI model — is the durable competitive advantage. Relevant for anyone justifying AI budgets or designing a CDP-first strategy.

stories.head: ZoomInfo GTM Studio audience creation grows 7x as teams consolidate go-to-market stacks
stories.plain: ZoomInfo reports a sevenfold quarter-on-quarter jump in audiences built inside GTM Studio, with five times more new users. The figures signal that B2B teams are consolidating audience-building and campaign launch into one platform, squeezing out point-solution vendors — a meaningful shift in how marketing AI is bought.

stories.head: iPullRank formalizes enterprise AI Search partnership with Profound, targeting GEO at scale
stories.plain: Agency iPullRank becomes a formal Profound partner, using Profound's citation and visibility data to help enterprise brands track and improve their appearance inside AI-generated search answers. This is a concrete example of GEO becoming a billable agency service, signalling a new budget line in enterprise marketing plans.

stories.head: SalesCloser deploys autonomous AI voice agents for applicant screening at a top-5 social platform
stories.plain: SalesCloser's autonomous AI agents now conduct voice-based applicant qualification at enterprise scale for a major social platform, integrating directly into existing workflow systems. This is a live, production agentic deployment — not a pilot — showing how decisioning agents are moving into high-volume HR and sales pipelines.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab ships AAMP 2.3: governance and privacy controls to move AI ad agents into production
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab's AAMP 2.3 standard adds human approval thresholds on ad spend and privacy controls specifically designed for AI agents running live campaigns. This is an industry-body specification, not a vendor product — it sets the rules that buyers and sellers must follow, directly shaping how agentic ad buying gets built and governed across the market.

stories.head: ADA acquires Algonomy to close gap from data insight to fully agentic retail experience
stories.plain: ADA has completed its purchase of Algonomy, a specialist in agentic decisioning for retail. The combined platform covers 34 markets across APAC, US, MENA, and Europe. It matters because it shows consolidation of the data-to-decision stack: one platform to collect customer data, decide what to do, and act — removing the need for separate point tools.

stories.head: AI speeds marketing production but teams still measure clicks, not business outcomes
stories.plain: A broad look at how AI is accelerating content and campaign production while measurement practices haven't kept up — most teams still track clicks rather than revenue or lifetime value. This gap makes it hard to justify AI investment to leadership and risks optimizing for the wrong thing, which is a critical issue for anyone buying or governing marketing AI.

stories.head: How to measure marketing when AI owns discovery — updating analytics for GEO
stories.plain: As AI answers replace traditional search results at the top of the funnel, standard click-based analytics become blind spots. The piece explains how to track brand visibility inside AI-generated responses and capture buyer intent before a user ever reaches your site — directly relevant to anyone building or buying measurement tools in a GEO-first world.

stories.head: Attentive 2026 report: personalized experiences are now a baseline shopper expectation, not a differentiator
stories.plain: A survey of 1,050 shoppers across the US, UK, and Australia finds that personalization has shifted from a nice-to-have to a purchase driver — consumers expect it and punish brands that miss. The data sets a concrete benchmark for what 1:1 messaging needs to deliver in 2026, influencing how CEPs and AI decisioning tools are evaluated and purchased.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Rewriting the Job Description of Marketing
body: The dominant signal this month is that AI is no longer a tool marketers use — it is increasingly an actor marketers direct. From Unanet embedding Champ agents across its entire ERP & CRM portfolio to ADA acquiring Algonomy to build a fully agentic growth platform, the architectural bet is clear: autonomous agents handling qualification, personalisation, and demand generation end-to-end.

This shifts the required skill from content production to agent orchestration — knowing how to set goals, guard-rails, and success criteria for systems that act on your behalf. Marketers who treat this as a new UI will be outrun by those who redesign workflows around delegation rather than automation.

themes.head: Measurement Gaps Are the Real AI Liability
body: AI is accelerating content output and audience targeting, but the month's coverage converges on a painful mismatch: measurement frameworks have not kept pace. When AI owns discovery — as explored in how to measure marketing when AI owns discovery — standard last-click and even multi-touch attribution models become structurally blind to the journeys that actually convert.

The Agile Brand piece on the AI ROI trap frames this sharply: proprietary first-party data is the only durable signal left, because it is the one asset AI intermediaries cannot absorb and redistribute. Teams that invest now in data infrastructure rather than just model access will have something to measure with when everyone else is flying blind.

themes.head: The Stack Consolidation Wave Is Accelerating
body: ZoomInfo's GTM Studio reporting a 7× growth in audience creation as teams consolidate their stack is not a product win story — it is a structural signal. Go-to-market teams are collapsing point solutions into unified platforms that can share a single data model, and vendors that sit at the centre of that model are capturing outsized usage.

This consolidation pressure also explains the ADA–Algonomy acquisition and the SalesCloser enterprise win: buyers want fewer contracts, tighter data loops, and one place where AI context accumulates. For marketers evaluating vendors, the question is no longer feature parity but which platform will become the data gravity well for their stack.
ev: Agile Brand · Re-architecting SaaS Demand Gen

themes.head: AI Discovery Channels Demand New Trust Signals
body: Yelp piping reviews into ChatGPT and IAB Tech Lab releasing standards to make AI agents ready for real advertising are two sides of the same structural shift: AI systems are becoming primary discovery surfaces, and the inputs those systems trust — reviews, structured data, authoritative citations — are now marketing real estate. iPullRank formalising an enterprise AI search partnership signals that agencies are already building practices around this.

Simultaneously, the accessibility piece from AudioEye highlights a risk: AI-generated digital experiences can quietly exclude users, creating both legal exposure and brand trust damage. Marketers need a trust strategy that spans optimising for AI discovery on the outside and auditing AI-built experiences on the inside.

MarTech · IAB Tech Lab AI agents for advertising

themes.head: First-Party Data Infrastructure Becomes the Uncopiable Moat
body: Two separate MarTech pieces this month make essentially the same argument from different angles: the only sustainable competitive advantage in an AI-saturated market is data no competitor can replicate. Milvus 3.0 going lake-native and SecuPi hardening database activity monitoring before AI amplifies risk are both infrastructure bets — the market is pricing in a future where vector search over proprietary data is a core marketing capability, not a data-science experiment.

The practical implication is a portfolio reallocation decision: budget that previously went to renting audience access through third-party platforms should increasingly flow toward owning the pipelines, storage, and governance layers that make first-party data actionable at AI speed. Teams that make this shift now will have a compounding asset; those that do not will find themselves paying rent forever.

month.takeaway: Across every story this month, the underlying bet is the same: teams that own their data infrastructure and learn to direct AI agents will compound advantages that pure model-renters cannot replicate.
